sections.label: Prepare block roots
sections.description: A Hadamard starts each of 256 four-wire blocks. Only q0, q4, q8 and the other block roots can read 1.

sections.label: Pair neighbors
sections.description: Each root controls its neighbor. Within each block the first two wires always agree.

sections.label: Extend each block
sections.description: Each block now reads 0000 or 1111. In the joint samples, the rightmost eight bits contain the first two blocks.

sections.label: Rotate each block
sections.description: A ZPow on the last wire of each block adds 45 degrees of phase to 1111. All 256 blocks remain independent.

sections.label: Bridge two blocks
sections.description: The CNOT from q3 to q4 joins the first two blocks. q4 and q5 now disagree half the time. Remove this CNOT and run again to restore their agreement.
